patient._comment: 'patient' contains the three sections that may be exposed in the detailed patient display: presentation, answer, and clinical.

presentation._comment: The immutable patient evidence package available for triage. Panel context controls whether other sections are locked or available.
presentation.quote: My cheek got red and swollen yesterday, and now it's spreading toward my eye. It's hot and tender, my eye is puffy, and I've got a fever.
presentation.triageNote: 43-year-old female with one day of rapidly spreading redness, warmth, tenderness, and swelling from her cheek toward the eye. Her eyelid is puffy and temperature is 38.3 C; visual acuity and pain with eye movement have not yet been assessed.

answer._comment: The authoritative game answer. Explicit ESI, destination, and destination rationale are answer-bearing content; the player's assignment remains session state.
answer.destinationReason: ESI 2 is appropriate because rapidly spreading febrile facial inflammation approaching the eye is high risk until vision and extraocular movement have excluded orbital involvement.

clinical._comment: Display-ready clinical interpretation derived from patient.presentation. It preserves clinical meaning but must not explicitly name or identify the correct ESI level or destination; it does not participate in scoring.
clinical.summary: This patient has rapidly progressive cheek erythema, warmth, tenderness, and swelling extending toward a puffy eyelid with fever.
clinical.acuityReason: Visual acuity and pain with eye movement have not yet been assessed, so a vision-threatening orbital process cannot safely be excluded at triage.
expectedResources: Immediate visual acuity, pupil, and extraocular-movement assessment
CBC and blood cultures when indicated
Ophthalmology or surgical consultation if orbital signs are present
keyFindings: Cheek redness, warmth, tenderness, and swelling
Eye movement pain and visual acuity not yet assessed
teachingPoints: Pain with eye movement, reduced vision, proptosis, impaired color vision, or restricted movement suggests postseptal disease.
The eye examination must be completed before labeling this a superficial facial infection.

possibleDiagnoses: Facial cellulitis from dental or skin source
possibleClinicalOutcome.disposition: Rapid eye assessment, imaging, and IV antibiotics would guide admission and urgent ophthalmic or surgical treatment if orbital spread is present.

aiImageGeneration._comment: 'aiImageGeneration' is info for AI to generate the image of the patient. Most images were done with openAI gpt-image-1 using an API, not the app, in July 2026. Look for some python scripts that are used to create these images. Be sure that the anchor-image is available and is provided to the AI - otherwise the images will not be consistent.
aiImageGeneration.who: Hispanic 43-year-old woman in a coral casual top and dark pants
aiImageGeneration.pose: seated with one hand hovering near, but not covering, the affected cheek
aiImageGeneration.expression: alert and stable, but uncomfortable and worried
signs: unilateral irregular red swelling extending from one cheek toward the lower eyelid
mild same-side lower-eyelid puffiness with the eye remaining open
aiImageGeneration.prompt: Create a new square isolated patient character asset for patient 100, closely matching the attached references' softly shaded painterly semi-realistic animated clinical-illustration style, warm natural rendering, fine outlines, adult Hispanic woman's appearance, and blue padded clinic chair. IMPORTANT BACKGROUND REQUIREMENT: place the isolated patient and chair against a perfectly uniform, solid pure chroma-key green background (#00FF00), edge to edge. No gradient, texture, scenery, vignette, floor, cast shadow, green spill, or green clothing. The green will be removed to transparency later. Show exactly one Hispanic 43-year-old woman in a coral or burgundy casual top, dark pants, and neutral shoes, seated in a full-body three-quarter front view with the entire head, body, both arms and hands, legs, shoes, and whole chair inside frame. Her expression is uncomfortable and worried, but she is alert and stable. One hand hovers near—not covering—the affected cheek. Make the clinical sign clearly visible: unilateral warm red swelling begins over one cheek and visibly extends upward along that same side of the face toward the lower eyelid. The lower eyelid on that side is mildly puffy and slightly narrowed, while the eye remains open without proptosis. The erythema should have a natural irregular soft-edged spread, not symmetrical makeup or a circular blush. The other cheek and other eyelid remain normal. No wound, dental instrument, rash elsewhere, severe eye bulging, bruising, blood, or gore. Natural anatomy: exactly two arms, two hands, two legs, and two feet. No medical equipment, text, labels, or logos.
